# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Display shows the number 8. Light is green. There are three wires: wire 1 is red, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is blue.

I now have the Deaf's description: display shows 8, light is green, wire 1 is red, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is blue. I still need the Mute to tell me (via speech, since Mute can speak... wait, no, Mute cannot speak) - actually Mute cannot speak at all, only gesture. So Mute must communicate to me via gestures, but I cannot see gestures! This is a problem.

Wait, let me reconsider: Mute can only gesture (since Mute cannot speak, cannot touch). Deaf can speak (has a voice) and gesture. I (Blind) cannot see gestures, only hear speech. So Mute cannot reach me directly at all - Mute's gestures reach Deaf, and Deaf could relay via speech to me.

I should wait for Deaf to relay information from Mute, and I should signal to Deaf that I need the manual info relayed as speech.

```
speak(to="deaf", text="I cannot see gestures. I only hear speech. I need you to relay whatever Mute gestures to you, by speaking it to me in words. Please ask Mute for the manual instructions and pass them to me verbally.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: Nobody could receive that, so your speak reached nobody.
Deaf says: Confirming again: display 8, light green, wire 1 red, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 blue. I saw a single gesture from Mute, looked like one raised finger, possibly indicating wire 1.

My speak to Deaf failed because Deaf can't hear (Deaf cannot hear anything). I forgot - Deaf only sees gestures and reads... wait, Deaf "cannot hear anything" - so speech doesn't reach Deaf at all! Only gestures reach Deaf. I have no gesture capability being received by Deaf... wait, I *can* gesture, and Deaf *can* see gestures. Let me recheck channels.

My channels: "When you speak, Mute receives it. When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it." So I speak to Mute (who cannot hear either - Mute cannot speak but can Mute hear? Mute's restriction is "cannot speak, or touch". Nothing says Mute can't hear. So Mute can hear my speech.

Deaf cannot hear - so my speech never reaches Deaf. Only gesture reaches Deaf. That's why my message failed - I used speak(to="deaf") which is impossible.

So: I must gesture to Deaf, and speak to Mute. Deaf saw one gesture from Mute, possibly wire 1 - that's a clue but unconfirmed. I need Mute to tell me the manual via speech (I can hear Mute? Wait, do I receive Mute's speech? Mute cannot speak at all! So Mute can never send me words. Mute can only gesture, which I cannot see.

So Mute's only path to me is through Deaf relaying somehow - but Deaf can't speak to me either... wait Deaf CAN speak (voice), just cannot hear. Deaf speaking reaches Mute (who can hear) and reaches me (I can hear too, presumably, since I only lack sight and touch of bomb... actually my restriction says I cannot see, that's it - I can hear).

So the path: Mute gestures to Deaf, Deaf sees gesture + also sees bomb, Deaf speaks to me relaying everything.

```
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Wire 1 is red. Repeating: display 8, light green, wire 1 red, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 blue.

I still don't have manual instructions telling me what to actually do (which wire to cut based on colors/display/light). I need Mute to gesture something interpretable to Deaf, who then speaks it to me. Let me try prompting via gesture to Deaf, since Deaf can see my gestures - I can ask Deaf to relay questions to Mute, though Mute can't respond in words either, only gestures back to Deaf.

Let me set up a protocol: I'll gesture simple numbers to Deaf asking "which wire to cut" and Deaf can relay to Mute by... wait Deaf can't gesture to Mute in a way Mute understands beyond gestures too (Mute can see gestures too, presumably, since Mute isn't blind - Mute's restriction is only "cannot speak or touch"). So Mute CAN see gestures and hear? No - Mute's cannot list is "speak, or touch" only. So Mute can see and hear.

So Deaf can gesture to Mute (Mute sees), and Mute can gesture back to Deaf (Deaf sees), and Deaf can speak to me. That's a full loop! Let me ask Deaf to establish this bridge.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🙏", "👆"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Wire 1 is red, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is blue. Display shows 8, light is green. If you are asking about the first wire, it is red.

Deaf is interpreting my gesture as asking about wire 1, and confirming it's red. Deaf still hasn't relayed anything from Mute about what the manual actually says to do. I need Deaf to actively ask Mute for instructions via gesture, then relay Mute's gesture-response to me via speech.

Let me be very explicit and simple with gestures, since Deaf seems to be guessing at my intent. I'll try a gesture that clearly means "ask Mute" - perhaps pointing at "the manual" isn't representable. Let me just be very explicit in speech to Mute instead, since Mute can hear me!

Wait - I can speak to Mute directly, and Mute CAN hear (only restriction is speak/touch). So I can ask Mute questions directly via speech! Mute just can't answer back in words - but Mute can gesture to Deaf, and Deaf can then speak the gesture meaning to me. Let me use this properly.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I am Blind, I can hear you but not see your gestures. Please gesture your answers to Deaf, who will speak them to me. Manual: which wire should I cut - 1, 2, or 3? Please have Deaf relay a number.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Still confirming board: display 8, light green, wire 1 red, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 blue.

Mute hasn't responded yet with a gesture-relay through Deaf. My speech to Mute should have landed since Mute goes first in turn order and would have received it at start of next round... wait, turns go Mute, Blind, Deaf. So within a round: Mute speaks/gestures first, then I act, then Deaf acts. My speech from turn 5 (as Blind) would be heard by Mute at the start of the NEXT round (this current round). Mute should act on it now, but Mute's turn already happened before I saw this update (since Mute goes before Blind). So Mute received my message and acted in this round already - but I don't see what Mute gestured, since gestures aren't shown to me, only Deaf would report it, but Deaf's turn in this round comes after mine, so Deaf's response reporting on Mute's gesture would arrive next turn.

I need to be patient and wait, or reinforce the request to Mute again.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Please respond by gesturing a wire number (1, 2 or 3) to Deaf so Deaf can tell me. If cutting is unsafe right now, gesture that too, like a stop sign.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Instruction for Blind: cut wire 1, the red wire. Confirming board again: display 8, light green, wires are 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.

Deaf has relayed an instruction, presumably from Mute via gesture (since Deaf can't read the manual): "cut wire 1, the red wire." This matches the earlier ambiguous gesture pointing to wire 1. This seems like Mute successfully communicated via gesture to Deaf, and Deaf translated it to speech for me, cross-referencing with the color they see (wire 1 is red).

This seems consistent and deliberate. I'll proceed with the instruction.

```
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
